{{Short description|American mathematician (1930–2021)}}

'''Martin Schechter''' (1930, [[Philadelphia]] – June 7, 2021) was an American mathematician whose work concerned [[mathematical analysis]] (specially [[partial differential equation]]s and [[functional analysis]] and their applications to [[mathematical physics]]). He was a professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{cite web |title=REMEMBERING PROFESSOR MARTIN SCHECHTER |url=https://ps.uci.edu/news/2438 |publisher=University of California, Irvine |access-date=19 August 2021}}</ref>

Schechter did his undergraduate studies at the [[City University of New York]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://www.math.uci.edu/~mschecht/vita.html|title=Curriculum vitae: Martin Schechter|accessdate=2015-10-31|archive-date=2021-06-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629184350/https://www.math.uci.edu/~mschecht/vita.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

He obtained his Ph.D. in 1957 from [[New York University]] (NYU) with [[Louis Nirenberg]] and [[Lipman Bers]] as thesis advisors; his dissertation was entitled ''On estimating partial differential operator in the L<sub>2</sub>-norm''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=13456}}</ref>
He taught at NYU from 1957 to 1966, and at [[Yeshiva University]] from 1966 to 1983, before moving to UC Irvine.<ref name="cv"/>

He is the author of several books, including the textbook ''Principles of Functional Analysis'' (Academic Press, 1971; 2nd ed., [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]], 2002).<ref>Review of ''Principles of Functional Analysis'', 2nd ed., by [[Robert G. Bartle]] (2002), {{MR|1861991}}.</ref>

Schechter was a member of the [[Association of Orthodox Jewish Scientists]].

Schechter is buried in the Har Menuchot cemetery in the Givat Shaul neighborhood of Jerusalem, Israel.

==Selected publications==
*Principles of Functional Analysis, Academic Press 1971, 2nd edition, American Mathematical Society 2002
*Minimax systems and critical point theory, Springer 2009
*with Wenming Zou: Critical point theory and its applications, Springer 2006
*Linking methods in critical point theory, Birkhäuser 1999
*Introduction to nonlinear analysis, Cambridge University Press 2004
*Operator methods in quantum mechanics, North Holland 1981, Dover 2002
*Spectra of partial differential operators, North Holland, 1971, 2nd edition 1986
*Modern methods in partial differential equations, McGraw Hill 1977
*with Lipman Bers and [[Fritz John]]; with supplements by [[Lars Gårding]], [[Arthur Milgram]]: [https://books.google.com/books?id=O_C2BgAAQBAJ Partial Differential Equations], Wiley 1964, 1966, American Mathematical Society 1991 (chapter by Schechter, Bers [https://books.google.com/books?id=O_C2BgAAQBAJ&pg=PA133 ''Elliptic Equations and Their Solutions''], pp. 131–149)
